title: sse: fix streaming chunking & framing for partial JSON, delimiter ordering, and token-event sequencing
author: Aisha Patel
body: Context: A regression introduced by the streaming refactor allowed SSE chunk delimiter tokens and partial-JSON token events to be emitted in a non-deterministic order which broke OpenAI-compatible clients, function/tool-calling flows, and structured-output consumers. This PR fixes the chunking/framing state machine so partial JSON objects are emitted with stable delimiter placement and strict token/event ordering; it also tightens EOSE (end-of-stream) semantics for the OpenAI compatibility layer. Motivation: production incidents where downstream parsers returned JSON parse errors or dropped function calls during streaming. Changes: 1) deterministic token/event sequencing in the SSE emitter; 2) atomic delimiter emission and reworked partial-json buffer flush; 3) sanitizer for trailing commas when streaming structured output; 4) updates to the openai-compat adapter to preserve event ordering for function/tool-calling messages; 5) extensive unit and e2e tests and a small performance regression check. Testing & QA checklist: [x] repro + minimal reproducer; [x] unit tests for serializer and emitter; [x] integration tests with openai-compat adapter; [x] e2e test in redwood-examples; [x] perf sanity check (<3% median latency regression); [x] changelog entry. Risk & compatibility: backwards-compatible for existing consumers (no breaking-change flagged); potential hot path allocation increase mitigated by reuse buffers. Release notes: see release_notes field. Related: ENG-2199 (incident followup), ENG-2230 (openai compat streaming work).
commits: fix(sse): stabilize token/event ordering in emitter - enforce sequence numbers and single-threaded flush
fix(serializer): atomic delimiter emission and partial-json buffer flush to avoid trailing-comma states
feat(openai-compat): preserve sse event ordering for function/tool-calls and structured output consumers
test(streaming): add unit tests for partial-json scenarios and delimiter edge-cases
test(e2e): add streaming validator harness in redwood-examples to catch cross-language parsing issues
chore: update changelog and add release notes
review_thread: Miguel Santos (2026-02-19): Found a repro using the TS SDK + node consumer; suggested a deterministic seq-id approach rather than relying on goroutine flush ordering.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-19): Reproduced locally and added reproducer in redwood-examples. Implemented seq-id queue and single-flush driver; pushed commit 1.
Jordan Kim (2026-02-20): Asked for microbenchmarks to ensure no latency regression; requested reuse of buffers to avoid allocations on hot path.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-20): Added buffer pooling and perf sanity check; attached numbers in CI artifacts (median +1.6% token latency, p95 unchanged).
Priya Menon (2026-02-22): Noted an edge-case when a client closes mid-chunk; requested clearer EOSE semantics in openai-compat adapter.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-23): Updated adapter to emit final partial payloads with explicit EOSE event, added tests for mid-chunk closes.
Jordan Kim (2026-02-24): Approves after tests and perf check. Miguel Santos (2026-02-24): Approves. Priya Menon (2026-02-24): Approves. Maintainer merged via squash on 2026-02-25.
ci_checks: unit-tests (go): failed on first run (race condition in tests) -> fixed and passed
e2e (examples validator): flaky first run -> rerun passed
perf-check: pass (median token latency +1.6%, p95 within SLO)
release_notes: Fix: SSE streaming chunking and framing - deterministic token/event ordering, partial-JSON delimiter fixes, improved OpenAI compatibility for streaming function/tool-calls. Backwards compatible; reduces streaming JSON parse errors for clients.
notes: This PR addresses a customer-impacting regression (incident ENG-2199). We recommend monitoring streaming error rates and function-calling drop rates for two releases after deploy; dashboards updated to include sse.parser.error_count metric.
